title: Cap. X Arg. III close: 'not being a sheep' is antecedent to not believing — Augustine: not of my sheep because predestined to everlasting ruin, not bought for eternal life by his blood
pass_a_gloss: Not to be a sheep in these words is considered as antecedent unto not believing: But what else is Not to be a sheep than not to be predestined, or to be rejected from the grace of the predestined, as Augustine explains, Tract. 48. in Evang. Joan. in these words, How therefore did he say unto those, YE ARE NOT OF MY SHEEP? Because he saw them predestined unto everlasting destruction, not purchased unto everlasting life by the price of his blood.
pass_b_english: In these words, not being a sheep is treated as antecedent to not believing. And what else is not being a sheep than not being predestined — or being rejected from the predestined's grace? So Augustine explains (Tract. 48. on John's Gospel): How then did he say to them, "YOU ARE NOT OF MY SHEEP"? Because he saw them predestined to everlasting ruin, not purchased for eternal life by the price of his blood.
source_text: Non esse ovem hisce in verbis consideratur ut antecedaneum ad non credere: At quid aliud est Non esse ovem quam non esse praedestinatum, vel esse a gratia praedestinatorum rejectum, ut explicat Augustinus, Tract. 48. in Evang. Joan. hisce verbis, Quomodo ergo istis dixit, NON ESTIS EX OVIBUS MEIS? Quia videbat eos ad sempiternum interitum praedestinatos, non ad vitam aeternam sui sanguinis pretio comparatos.
